personality_traits: Oblivious/self-absorbed — stays glued to the TV soccer match through the whole cold open, feet up on the coffee table, ignoring his wife entering the room
Impulsive and reflex-driven — his body reacts to the goal on screen (lunging, shouting) before his mind registers what is actually happening around him
Belatedly caring — once he processes that his wife is unresponsive, he snaps into concern, repeating her name and 'are you okay?'
Comedically dense — the gap between his celebratory reaction and the seriousness of his wife's collapse is played for deadpan absurdist comedy
emotional_range: bored/half-checked-out contentment (slouched on couch, snacking, half-watching TV)
manic triumphant joy (mid-celebration, sprawled on the floor)
confusion/dawning alarm (realizing his wife is on the ground beneath him)

lurches forward off the couch and drops to his knees on the floor at the moment of the goal
throws both arms/hands down onto the rug on either side of Jane's body mid-celebration, effectively pinning/straddling her without noticing

characters.interactions_notes: He never makes eye contact with Jane until after his celebration — his attention triangulates entirely on the television, and she enters his physical space (or he ends up on top of her) as a side effect of his goal celebration rather than an intentional acknowledgment of her. The power dynamic in the scene is that his enthusiasm/priorities (the match) physically and narratively steamroll her workload (laundry, chores) until the joke pivots and he is forced to confront her sudden collapse right in front of him.

characters.name_or_role: Jane (wife, dark bun hairstyle, brown top and dark skirt)
personality_traits: Weary and put-upon — enters mid-chore, arms full of folded laundry and a snack bag, suggesting she's the one managing the household while he watches TV
Wry/unimpressed — her raised eyebrow and sidelong glance at him convey silent judgment rather than confrontation

Physically depleted by the end of the clip — collapses to the floor, becoming completely limp and unresponsive, consistent with the video's 'low battery' framing (running on empty from unacknowledged effort)
emotional_range: mild, resigned exasperation (entering the room, glancing at him)
flat neutrality/exhaustion while walking past him
complete shutdown — eyes rolled back/unfocused, mouth slack, motionless once on the ground
expressions: 0:00 — one eyebrow cocked, eyes narrowed slightly toward her husband as she walks past him with the laundry — a look of tired tolerance
mid-scene — face goes slack, eyes half-open and unfocused, as she ends up collapsed on the rug amid scattered snacks/laundry
0:09-0:13 — eyes glassy, unmoving, mouth open in an inert, expressionless slump while he shouts over her and then asks if she's okay
gestures: walks briskly through the front door balancing a stack of folded blankets/towels topped with a chip bag against her chest
no acknowledgment of the husband as she crosses behind/beside the couch
collapses supine on the rug, arms splayed, legs limp, surrounded by dropped snacks and soda cans — full-body stillness contrasts with his frantic motion on top of her
characters.interactions_notes: Jane and her husband never actually converse before her collapse — she does the household labor silently while he is fixated on the screen, and their only direct physical contact comes when he inadvertently ends up sprawled over her during his goal celebration. The dynamic is asymmetric: her actions (chores) go unnoticed until her body literally shuts down, at which point he finally directs attention and words ('Jane!', 'are you okay?') toward her — the joke's structure implies her burnout was building unnoticed the whole time he was absorbed in the game.
